title: Max Hangs - One Arm 95%
texts:  Max Hangs - One Arm 95% Premium Workout
Single Arm Deadhangs – 10 second hangs at 95%

PLEASE COMPLETE A FINGER STRENGTH TESTING SESSION BEFORE STARTING THIS EXERCISE & A FULL WARM UP

The goal of this workout is to improve forearm and finger strength 

Complete the following 6 sets of hangs using a fingerboard or edge which is approximately 20mm deep. The edge used in training should be the same as that used in the finger strength testing session. Each set consists of 2 reps where each rep corresponds with either the left hand or the right hand followed by a 30s rest between the reps.  In total, 6 sets of 1x10s hang are completed on each hand. 

Progressively build up the load used during your warm up until you are ready to train at maximal intensity on this specific hold, grip type and body position. 

Sets 1-6 = 95% of maximal load scored in the 5 second finger strength self assessment. This is calculated as 95% of the total load (bodyweight & bodyweight adjustment via pulley). If you weigh 70kg and needed 10kg assistance to perform your one arm hang, the total load was 60kg. 95% would be equal to 0.95 x 60kg = 57kg. To bring your loading to 57kg you would need to do all training hangs with 13kg assistance (13 + 57 = 70kg).

Retest every 4-8 weeks to work out new loadings for this session. 

If you cannot complete the full 10 second hang, please reduce the weight until you can complete. Once the fingers or arm on any hang start to open out, put your feet on the floor immediately and do not continue to complete opening of fingers or arm.
